correctness.rationale: Write m=(a+b)/2 and d=(a−b)/2. Exactly four signed coordinate permutations of v=(a,b) become (αm,βd) independently with α,β∈{±1}. Input cube yields |m|+|d|=max{|a|,|b|}≤1; at each step greedy scalar sign against the current scalar prefix keeps |M_k|,|D_k|≤1 by |S−sign(S)x|≤max{|S|,|x|}. The inverse linear map (M,D)↦(M+D,M−D) sends the four invariant-square vertices to (±2,0),(0,±2). Convexity of every ℓ_q norm, including q=1 and q=∞, gives max≤2 on the entire square and ALL prefixes, with no lookahead. For v1=(1,1),v2=(1,−1), every admissible second prefix is a signed coordinate axis vector of magnitude 2; bound sharp for all q. Universal analytic proof, no numerical extrapolation.
residual_risks: Specific to two coordinates, input ℓ∞ cube, and per-vector sign+swap; higher dimension or p<∞ not established.

The constant 2 is uniform across the full q-range and sharp with a two-vector witness. The sign+swap representation decomposes into two scalar online sign games, explaining a nontrivial improvement by the factor 2^(1/q) over the stated general finite-q estimate. Not an unmotivated handpicked norm.
